input.quote: MSL agrees to protect, defend, hold harmless, and indemnify IBM from and against any and all claims, damages, liabilities, losses and expenses, arising out of the following, whether alleged or actual:
input.rationale: Section 15.1 gives us a full vendor-side defence and indemnity from MSL covering (a) third-party IP infringement (patent, trademark, copyright, mask work, trade secret) arising from MSL's performance or MSL-procured parts, designs, deliverables and pre-existing materials, (b) MSL's failure to comply with applicable law, and (c) MSL's failure to perform its warranty and support obligations — squarely the preferred position on IP, breach of law and MSL misconduct. The carve-outs are appropriately narrow and limited to claims caused by IBM-selected marks, IBM's written specifications or IBM-provided defective designs, i.e. our own inputs, rather than the broad "modification/combination" exclusions the fallback would tolerate. Section 15.2 contains only standard procedural conditions (prompt notice, cooperation, MSL control of defence with our right to participate at our own expense) and MSL's forward-looking cure options in 15.2(b) are at MSL's expense and do not displace its payment obligation or cap the indemnity. Appendix A item 5 adds a further MSL indemnity for Microsoft code matters in IBM's favour. There is no reciprocal IBM indemnity for MSL's services, so the direction of risk is correct. Minor points noted but not flagged: the indemnity does not expressly name a data-breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct prong, and 16.21 lets MSL suspend supply where a claim stems from IBM-specified designs — sub-elements short of preferred wording that do not affect the material terms.
